title: Retrieve a document by URL
description: Retrieve one indexed document you can open in Glean by its URL, then retrieve that same document by the document ID printed in the first response.

codeWalkthrough.intro: You sign in with @gleanwork/auth and call the experimental document endpoints over HTTP. The published TypeScript API client does not include these endpoints. client.documents is a different API.

examples.title: Call the experimental Documents API
examples.description: Find your Glean backend, take a documents:read token from the auth package, and send X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. GET /api/documents reads by URL. GET /api/documents/{document_id} reads by the document ID from the first response, with the path segment encoded.

examples.title: Round-trip the document ID
examples.description: Read the URL response, then request that document_id again. Require the same document_id. HTTP 404, which usually means your Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on, fails the command. The permalink in the response may differ from the URL you passed.

prerequisites: A Glean instance where you can open indexed documents
Your work email, or the complete Glean backend HTTPS origin
The documents:read OAuth scope, or a user-scoped API token created with documents:read (legacy label DOCUMENTS)

demoQueries.query: Retrieve a document URL you can open in Glean
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Prints the title, a document_id line, the permalink, datasource, document type, timestamps, and url_request_id, then a line that says Round-trip document_id matches. The permalink may differ from the URL you passed. HTTP errors, including 404, exit non-zero and do not print that success line. A 404 usually means your Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on. If they are on, a 404 usually means the document does not exist or you cannot access it. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support. With --content, the output also includes content_segments. An empty full_text_list still prints the document and means there is no extracted text.

codeAssets.description: TypeScript CLI that retrieves an indexed document by URL and then by the returned document ID

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Copy the runnable TypeScript CLI and its offline tests into a new directory. Sign-in uses the official `@gleanwork/auth` package.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Enter the project directory and install its dependencies. Run the remaining commands from this directory.

steps.title: Run the offline tests
steps.description: Run the tests. They do not use your Glean login or the network. Passing tests does not prove you can reach your Glean instance.

steps.title: Choose an authentication path
steps.description: OAuth is the default. `@gleanwork/auth` discovers your instance, registers the OAuth client dynamically, and stores credentials outside the project. If OAuth is unavailable, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, set `GLEAN_SERVER_URL`, and create a user-scoped API token with `documents:read` (legacy label `DOCUMENTS`). Put that token in `GLEAN_API_TOKEN` and skip the next step. Omit `--email` from the remaining commands. If email discovery finds the wrong instance, replace `--email` with `--server-url` and your complete backend HTTPS origin.

steps.title: Sign in with OAuth
steps.description: Run the login command with the `documents:read` scope and finish authorization in your browser. Wait until the command reports success. Skip this step when you configured a token in `.env`.

steps.title: Verify against your instance
steps.description: Retrieve one document you can open, then retrieve it again by the returned `document_id`. The command prints the permalink, title, datasource, and both request IDs. With a token in `.env`, omit `--email`.

steps.title: Request extracted text
steps.description: Run the same retrieval with `--content`. The client sends `include=CONTENT`, and the response adds `content.full_text_list`. An empty list means Glean has no extracted text. A failure to read requested content fails the command. With a token, omit `--email`.

questions.prompt: What is your work email address?
What is the URL of a document you can open in Glean?

architecture.label: Documents API
architecture.caption: experimental get by URL, then by ID

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the experimental document retrieve-by-URL quickstart. Ask for the work email and one document URL the person can open in Glean. Run the tests before authentication. Sign in with the official glean-auth CLI from @gleanwork/auth using the documents:read scope, or set GLEAN_SERVER_URL and a user-scoped GLEAN_API_TOKEN. When creating that token, choose documents:read (legacy label DOCUMENTS). Do not add a scope-fallback wrapper and do not request any other scope. The published @gleanwork/api-client package has no methods for these document endpoints. Do not call client.documents; that is a different API. Call the HTTP API with fetch. Send X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. A 404 usually means the Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support, and show the Request ID. If the endpoints are on, the document does not exist or you cannot access it. GET /api/documents?url= and read document plus request_id. Then GET /api/documents/{document_id} with the returned document_id, encoding the path segment, and require the same document_id. The response url is the permalink and may differ from the submitted URL. Pass include=CONTENT only when --content is set. CONTENT adds document.content.full_text_list. An empty list means no extracted text. A content failure fails the whole request. Exit non-zero on HTTP errors, including 404. For a Gmail or Outlook message, pass the message URL, not the ID from the search result or chat citation. That URL can still 404. Federated results and go links are not retrievable. On HTTP 403, list token scope and instance setup as possible causes. Do not teach per-item status enums. Print request IDs. Never log tokens.
llmContext: Use @gleanwork/auth 1.0.0 and the documents:read scope. The legacy token label is DOCUMENTS. @gleanwork/api-client has no methods for these document endpoints, and client.documents is a different API. Call fetch and send X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. GET /api/documents?url= then GET /api/documents/{document_id} and require the same document_id. Encode the path segment. include=CONTENT is optional and adds content.full_text_list. HTTP 404 usually means the endpoints are off. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support. If they are on, the document does not exist or you cannot access it. For Gmail and Outlook, pass the message URL. Federated results and go links are not retrievable. On 403, name scope and instance setup. Do not log tokens or teach per-item status enums.

content.problem: A search result or chat citation gives you a document URL. To see the title, permalink, and extracted text for that one document, you call Glean's experimental document endpoints, then confirm the document ID in the response reads back the same document. The published TypeScript API client does not include these endpoints, so this quickstart calls the HTTP API and uses the official auth package for sign-in.
takeItFurther: Pass --content when you need extracted text. include=CONTENT adds content.full_text_list. An empty list means Glean stored no extracted text. You still see the document. If Glean cannot read the text you asked for, the command fails.

Use the batch recipe when you have many document IDs and URLs. Copy the document_id line this command prints and pass it to --id there. The batch prints documents Glean returns under results, and document IDs or URLs it does not return under warnings.
Keep the document_id this command prints. The get-by-id call accepts that ID. For a Gmail or Outlook message, pass the message URL, not the ID from the search result or chat citation.

guardrails.title: Keep the experimental header on every request
guardrails.rule: This client sets X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. Keep that header if you add a call. A 404 with the header usually means your Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support.

guardrails.title: Request only documents:read
guardrails.rule: OAuth login and the token provider use the documents:read scope. Do not add other scopes. If you create an API token instead, choose documents:read (legacy label DOCUMENTS).

guardrails.title: Treat HTTP 404 as a failed command
guardrails.rule: HTTP 404 exits non-zero and does not print Round-trip document_id matches. It usually means your Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support, and share the Request ID. If the endpoints are on, a 404 usually means the document does not exist or you cannot access it. The batch command lists a missing document ID or URL under warnings and still exits 0.

limitations.title: Experimental endpoints
limitations.description: These endpoints are experimental and can change. This client sends X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. If your Glean instance has not turned the endpoints on, you still get HTTP 404. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support. The published @gleanwork/api-client package has no methods for these endpoints. client.documents reads documents through a different API. Do not call it here.

limitations.title: Some documents cannot be retrieved
limitations.description: A Gmail or Outlook search result or chat citation can show an ID that only works in that result. Pass the message URL instead of that ID. The URL can still return 404. Go links and federated search results cannot be retrieved. You only get documents you can open.

limitations.title: Content is extracted text, not the file
limitations.description: include=CONTENT adds content.full_text_list. An empty list means Glean stored no extracted text. You still see the document. If Glean cannot read the text you asked for, the command fails instead of printing the document without content. The command prints a short preview, not every segment.
